intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Heterozygosity for a nonsense mutation in the NECTIN1 gene has been associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7) in northern Venezuela.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous loss-of-function mutations of the poliovirus receptor-like 1 (PVRL1) gene encoding nectin-1.
checks.explanation: PVRL1 is the former symbol for NECTIN1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. A gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature that restates the paper's gene identification, so the claim is accepted.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a nonsense mutation in the NECTIN1 gene has been associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7) in northern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract links heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X to sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P. NECTIN1 is the approved symbol for PVRL1, and OFC7 is the OMIM label for this condition, so both are standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder. Suzuki et al. (1998) listed its features as unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate. Some reported patients have also had mental retardation (Zlotogora et al., 1987; Rodini and Richieri-Costa, 1990).

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families, who were probably related to each other, from a relatively isolated, inbred population on Margarita Island (Nueva Esparta State) in northeastern Venezuela. All had ectodermal dysplasia along with other anomalies. Females were affected as severely as males, and expressivity varied. The authors concluded that the clinical picture did not fit any known ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Yoshida et al. (2015) found a homozygous c.400C-T transition in exon 2 of the PVRL1 (NECTIN1) gene in a 7-year-old Japanese boy with CLPED1.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of exon 2 of PVRL1 revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*).
checks.explanation: A C>T change is a transition by definition, and the abstract places it in exon 2. The boy's age and Japanese origin are stated elsewhere in the abstract.

checks.claim: The Japanese boy with CLPED1 and the homozygous PVRL1 c.400C-T mutation was the first child of a consanguineous marriage.
checks.evidence_quote: A 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage,

checks.claim: The PVRL1 c.400C-T transition causes an arg134-to-ter (R134X) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*)
checks.explanation: p.Arg134* is the same change as R134X.

checks.claim: Both parents of the Japanese boy with CLPED1 were heterozygous for the PVRL1 c.400C-T (R134X) mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: His parents were heterozygous for the mutant alleles.

checks.claim: The predicted truncated protein from PVRL1 R134X lacks the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1.
checks.evidence_quote: All four PVRL1 mutations identified in cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome to date, including this study, resulted in truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1,
checks.explanation: The paper says this of all four mutations, including this one.

checks.claim: The transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1 are needed to start the cell-cell adhesion process.
checks.evidence_quote: lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1, which is necessary to initiate the cell-cell adhesion process.
